title: autotune: default batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Prior work introduced autotune recommendations for batching and caching, but defaults and quantization profiles were scattered across codepaths and the unit-econ tooling lacked an ergonomic CLI for ops and SREs. This PR unifies defaults, ships a small set of validated quantization profiles for common model families, and adds a unit-econ CLI and API endpoints so customers and internal teams can simulate cost/latency tradeoffs.

What I changed: consolidated default batching and KV cache heuristics into runtime/config/autotune; added three quantization profiles (int8, int4-fast, int4-accurate) with metadata, validation tests, and compatibility mapping to runtime kernels; implemented unit-econ tooling (CLI: redwood-uecon) that can ingest workload traces, run simulation across batching/quant/replica configs, and emit per-token cost and latency percentiles. Also added an internal API endpoint (/internal/uecon/simulate) for remote runs and a lightweight UI surface in Console for previewing recommended configs.

Key files changed (high-level): runtime/autotune/config.go, runtime/autotune/heuristics.go, models/quant/profiles.yaml, tools/uecon/cli/main.go, api/internal/uecon_handler.go, console/components/uecon-preview.jsx, tests/autotune_integration_test.go.

Backward compatibility: defaults are opt-in via new cluster config flag (autotune.defaults_enabled=true) for Dedicated and Private so we can ramp customers. Quant profiles are additive and require explicit selection; runtime will not change existing deployments unless users flip the flag.

Testing and validation: unit and integration tests added for heuristic convergence (tests/autotune_integration_test.go), quant profile validation test ensures kernel compatibility and model accuracy regression <1% on our eval set. CI ran full unit, integration, and e2e smoke tests. Staging run against a small Dedicated pool showed 18% cost reduction on our conversational workload with p95 latency change within SLO (p95 +12ms).

Rollout plan: feature-flag gated; start with internal beta, then canary to 10% of Dedicated customers, monitor cost/unit, latency p95/p99, and quality regression dashboards.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps simulation logic separate from serving hot path; runtime only reads compact profiles and heuristics to avoid allocations. Related: ENG-1423 (autotune roadmap), PM-067 (product impact study).

feat(quant): add quantization profiles (int8, int4-fast, int4-accurate) with validation
feat(uecon): add redwood-uecon CLI and internal simulation API
chore(console): add uecon preview component and minimal wiring
test: add integration tests for autotune convergence and quant profile validation
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can we make the default flag off for Hosted to avoid any unexpected regressions? Also please document expected memory impact for int4 profiles.

Maya Chen: Agree on flag defaults — Hosted will remain opt-out and Dedicated/Private have opt-in cluster flag. Int4 profiles allocate a small 6% additional kv-cache metadata in the worst case; added note in docs and comments in heuristics.go.
Sofia Martinez: Integration tests are failing intermittently on CI (TestAutotuneConvergence). Looks like a race on the sampling window.
Maya Chen: Updated tests to use deterministic seed and extended the sampling window; added retry in the flaky path. Re-ran CI.
Liam O'Connor: Approving after test fixes and a successful staging run showing expected cost improvements. Please ensure rollout checklist is added to ENG-1423.
Maya Chen: Added rollout checklist to ENG-1423 and the PR release notes. Thanks!
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (flaky test fixed and rerun)
release_notes:
Add autotune defaults for batching and caching (opt-in), ship validated quantization profiles (int8, int4-fast, int4-accurate), and introduce unit-econ CLI + internal simulation API. Expected cost reduction ~15-25% for conversational workloads when enabled.

Migration: none required; feature gated behind cluster flags.
notes_for_ops: Enable via cluster flag: autotune.defaults_enabled=true. Run redwood-uecon simulate --trace sample_trace.json --profiles int4-fast,int8 to preview recommendations. Monitor uecon.cost_per_token and runtime.batch_size metrics after rollout.
qa_checklist: Run unit and integration tests locally (go test ./... -run TestAutotune)
Run redwood-uecon simulate against sample_trace.json and compare results to expected/benchmarks
Staging canary: enable flag on 10% Dedicated nodes and monitor p95 latency and quality dashboards
Verify quant profile compatibility by running model self-check (tools/quant/validate_profile)
